core_obligations: Neighbourhood chain: introduce condition (4), flatness of g^*F over S near x'; use that g is etale hence flat and open so that U' -> g(U') is a surjective flat map of neighbourhoods, giving (4) iff (1) by flatness permanence, and then use the affine identifications of global sections of g^*F, G and pi_*G to obtain (4) iff (2) iff (3) up to the displayed topological comparison of affine neighbourhoods (proof lines 706-730).

Local-ring chain setup: write the commutative diagram of local ring maps O_{X,x} -> O_{X',x'} -> O_{Z',z'} and O_{Y',y'} <- O_{Z',z'} with base rings O_{S,s} and O_{S',s'}, and use the local form of the etale up-and-down lemma to equate flatness over O_{S,s} and over O_{S',s'} throughout (proof lines 733-748).

Finish the local-ring chain: the map gamma is faithfully flat, so flatness of F_x over O_{S,s} is equivalent to flatness of g^*F_{x'} over O_{S',s'}, and since g^*F_{x'}, G_{z'} and pi_*G_{y'} are isomorphic as O_{S',s'}-modules by the finite-morphism-single-point-in-fibre lemma, all three local statements (a), (b), (c) are equivalent (proof lines 749-759).
proof_roadmap: Neighbourhood statement: reduce to the auxiliary condition (4) on g^*F through flatness and openness of the etale g, then compare the three modules through their affine global sections Gamma(X', g^*F) = Gamma(Z', G) = Gamma(Y', pi_*G) together with the topological comparison of affine neighbourhoods (proof lines 706-730).
Local-ring statement: set up the square of local ring maps and invoke the local form of the etale up-and-down lemma so that S and S' may be used interchangeably for flatness (proof lines 733-748).
Close the local chain by descent along the faithfully flat gamma and by the isomorphism of the three O_{S',s'}-modules g^*F_{x'}, G_{z'} and pi_*G_{y'} (proof lines 749-759).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the flatness companion of the finite presentation comparison: it equates flatness of F near x, of G near z' and of pi_*G near y' over the base, and then repeats the comparison at the three local rings (statement lines 691-702). What is non-formal is that the etale up-and-down lemma is used to move between flatness over S and over S' while the remaining comparisons are made through the affine global sections Gamma(X', g^*F) = Gamma(Z', G) = Gamma(Y', pi_*G), so that the module-theoretic statement about pi_*G is reduced to one about G on a finite cover (proof lines 718-730). In the local-ring chain the corresponding identification of g^*F_{x'}, G_{z'} and pi_*G_{y'} as O_{S',s'}-modules is what allows a single descent along the faithfully flat map gamma to settle all three statements at once (proof lines 749-759). Both chains are short and use only quoted inputs, which places the claim at H2.
